Reference Text: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. Pebble Spring spent the first few months observing the mortar and stone-laying techniques. They took notes in a small leather journal they had carved from a fallen branch. The local masons were friendly enough but occasionally suspicious of a tree-being wielding a glowing staff. Pebble Spring learned that houses required more than just walls and a roof. Doors, windows, and ventilation all played crucial roles in making a shelter livable. They practiced in the forest clearing behind the village, building small models at first. The arcane magic from their staff helped them shape wood and stone with surprising precision. By the second year, they were confident enough to attempt a full-sized structure. The village elder offered them a plot of land at the edge of the settlement. Pebble Spring was overjoyed and began gathering materials with great enthusiasm. They hauled timber from the nearby woods and collected stones from the riverbed. The foundation was laid on a warm spring morning, and the whole village came to watch. Children ran around the construction site, pointing at the glowing runes on the staff. Weeks turned into months as the walls rose higher and higher. Pebble Spring noticed that the mortar between the stones was not perfectly even in some areas. They worked to correct the inconsistencies, applying their arcane focus to blend the textures. The roof was the most challenging part, requiring careful angles and a strong frame. With a final wave of their staff, the last shingle fell into place with a satisfying thud. The house stood complete, a modest but sturdy dwelling that blended naturally with the landscape. They moved in on the very first day of the early autumn season and the whole neighborhood was quite impressed by how the mossy exterior seemed to grow naturally from the earth with a spotty paint finish that added character to the dwelling.
